results.title: How spicy is too spicy? Korea tests popular instant noodles
results.content: Spicy instant noodles in Korea range from mildly kicky to tear-inducingly hot — and some pack more than a full day’s worth of salt into a single bowl, according to a consumer report released Tuesday by the Korea Consumer Agency. The state-run watchdog conducted a comprehensive safety and quality assessment of 12 top-selling instant noodle products. The test group comprised seven traditional soup-based ramyeon products and five brothless, stir-fried varieties, evaluating them across key metrics including spiciness intensity, nutritional content, safety standards and retail pricing. Laboratory analysis revealed that the concentration of capsaicinoids — the natural chemical compounds in chili peppers responsible for their fiery burn — varied by nearly seven times among the tested brands. results.title: 'Honey trap': Nvidia spy scandal puts Korea on alert
results.content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a Chinese woman accused of spying for Beijing has emerged as a significant national security concern for the United States. According to U.S. intelligence officials, Alice Huang, who worked as a business executive at Singapore-based data center firm Megaspeed in 2023, allegedly collected intelligence and passed it on to China. The scandal erupted amid an intensifying race between the U.S. and China for global leadership in artificial intelligence (AI). The case has served as a wake-up call for South Korea. results.title: Students from 30 countries gather in Seoul to learn Korean language and culture
results.content: Ninety-two students and teachers from 30 countries wrapped up a five-day immersive camp hosted by the Ministry of Education. A group of 92 secondary school students and teachers from 30 countries completed a five-day immersive journey into Korean language and culture, concluding a nationwide youth camp organized by the Ministry of Education. To mark the end of the 2026 International Korean Education Youth Camp, the ministry and the International Korean Education Foundation held a celebratory ceremony Tuesday evening at Sarangjae, a traditional guest house on the National Assembly grounds in Seoul. Running from Friday to Tuesday across Seoul and Incheon, the camp brought together students enrolled in Korean language classes at their home schools. This year’s cohort welcomed its first-ever participant from Mexico, alongside students from Malaysia and Uzbekistan who were recently featured i

results.title: Shinsegae Q3 net income soars 146.4% to $88.5 mil.
results.content: Shinsegae Inc., the operator of Korea's major department store chain, on Tuesday reported its third-quarter net profit of 119 billion won ($88.5 million), a 146.4 percent jump from a year earlier. The retailer said in a regulatory filing that operating profit for the July-September period increased 64.7 percent on-year to 164.3 billion won. Revenue also inched up 1.2 percent to 1.65 trillion won. The earnings exceeded market expectations. The average estimate of net profit by analysts stood at 84.5 billion won, according to a survey by Yonhap Infomax, the financial data firm of Yonhap News Agency.

results.title: Ex-US diplomat says OPCON transfer may not move rapidly, cites 'no consensus' in Washington
results.content: A former U.S. diplomat said Tuesday that the envisioned transfer of wartime operational control (OPCON) from Washington to Seoul may not move forward swiftly, citing "no consensus" on the key alliance issue in the United States. Speaking virtually at a forum, Joseph Yun, former acting U.S. ambassador to South Korea and special representative for North Korea, also said that there is no consensus in Washington over Seoul's push to secure rights to enrich uranium for peaceful civilian purposes and acquire nuclear submarines. Yun offered his forecasts over what will happen during the remaining two years of U.S. President Donald Trump's administration, particularly in the wake of this month's U.S. midterm elections, in which Democrats won control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives. "I cannot imagine (the OPCON transfer efforts) moving very rapidly," Yun said during the forum

results.title: Seoul names 10 winners at inaugural 2026 Seoul Design Honors awards
results.content: Seoul named 10 individuals and companies as recipients of its inaugural Seoul Design Honors, recognizing projects that have improved public spaces, strengthened the city's identity and made everyday life safer and more accessible for residents. The Seoul Metropolitan Government held the first 2026 Seoul Design Honors ceremony Tuesday at City Hall, presenting mayoral commendations to four individuals and six companies selected from 49 nominations. The honors were established to recognize contributions to design development and encourage work that puts people at the center of urban design, drawing inspiration from two Korean cultural achievements: the angbuilgu, an ancient sundial, and "Hunminjeongeum," the original Korean alphabet. The individual recipients are Kim Hyun-jung, Jung Mi, Ahn Jang-won and Cho Yong-jun, all of whom have done work that has helped shape major public spaces and i

results.title: Genesis GV90 sets sights on BMW, Mercedes-Benz in full-size luxury SUV market
results.content: Genesis is stepping up competition in the full-size luxury SUV market with the full-electric GV90, taking aim at German rivals — BMW and Mercedes-Benz — as it seeks to carve out a bigger share of the lucrative high-end segment. The brand unveiled on Tuesday pricing for the GV90, its first full-size flagship SUV, starting at 139.5 million won ($103,000) in Korea. This places the vehicle in a similar price range to the BMW X7 and Mercedes-Benz GLS, positioning Genesis to compete directly for buyers who have traditionally favored German luxury SUVs. The launch represents a significant test for Genesis, which has spent years building its reputation as a premium brand, but has yet to establish the same level of recognition as BMW and Mercedes-Benz in the upper reaches of the luxury market. results.title: Seoul plant hospital admits 10,000 potted patients since 2023 opening
results.content: A city-run hospital for houseplants? Welcome to modern Seoul. Seoul’s dedicated emergency room for sickly flora has administered 10,886 diagnoses, treatments and house-call consultations since opening its doors in 2023, the Seoul Metropolitan Government said Tuesday. Nestled inside the Seoul Agricultural Technology Center in Seocho District, the Companion Plant Hospital functions like a full-scale medical center for dramatic greenery. Resident plant doctors diagnose bug infestations and mysterious wilting, prescribing everything from targeted pesticides to emergency repotting. Plants needing intensive care can even be admitted for up to three months of inpatient recovery, while anxious plant parents leave with tailored home-care prescriptions. results.title: Seoul's Namdaemun Market to host K-food night festival with star chefs
results.content: Namdaemun Market, one of Seoul’s oldest and most bustling traditional markets, is opening its doors after dark for an eight-day night food festival starting Saturday, the Seoul Metropolitan Government said Tuesday. Running daily from 6 p.m. to 9 p.m. through Nov. 21, the Seoul Moonlight Gastronomy Festival will transform the market’s covered arcade near Sungnyemun — the historic city gate commonly known as Namdaemun — into a vibrant nocturnal dining hub. The daytime landmark, which draws around 300,000 visitors daily, usually quiets down after dusk. The festival’s centerpiece is a pop-up tavern reimagined in the style of a "jumak" — a traditional Joseon Dynasty (1392–1910) roadside inn where travelers once gathered for food, drink and conversation. results.title: Army temporarily grounds Apache helicopters amid US inspection for possible defect
results.content: The Korean Army has temporarily grounded its Apache military helicopters as U.S. authorities began inspections on the fleet over a possible malfunction of their transmission system, an Army official said Tuesday. The grounding of the AH-64E Apache Guardian attack helicopters has been in place since early October, after the Army received a safety advisory from the U.S. military regarding the transmission component, Army spokesperson Capt. Bae Seok-jin said in a press briefing. "As a safety precaution, the Army temporarily grounded the fleet in early October (for the U.S. side) to conduct technical inspections in phases," Bae said. "Operations will resume sequentially based on the inspection results." results.title: Top 10 firms take up over 60% of Korea's exports in Q3 amid chip boom
results.content: The share of Korea's top 10 exporters in the country's total outbound shipments rose sharply in the third quarter from a year earlier, data showed Tuesday, driven by strong demand for semiconductors and other technology products. Exports by the top 10 companies accounted for 60.9 percent of total exports in the July-September period, up from 40.5 percent a year earlier, according to data compiled by the Ministry of Data and Statistics. The country's top 100 exporters accounted for 79.4 percent of total exports in the third quarter, up from 67.9 percent a year earlier. Korea's total exports came to $318.6 billion in the third quarter, an increase of 72.3 percent on-year. By company size, exports by conglomerates more than doubled to $248.6 billion, while those by medium-sized companies rose 12.8 percent to $36.9 billion. results.title: [K-ART FOCUS] Yeon Jin-yeong challenges conventions of masculinity
results.content: A U.S. military uniform becomes a bathrobe. Combat boots take on the soft, playful look of jelly shoes. A military duffel bag becomes a Birkin-style handbag. A urinal is adorned with colorful beads, as though it, too, needs accessories to stand out. Bathroom mirrors are covered with images of male fashion models drawn from the artist's own Instagram feed. Inside a former military bathroom and shower at Camp Greaves in Paju, Gyeonggi Province, installation artist Yeon Jin-yeong gives symbols of military masculinity an unexpected makeover. Objects associated with toughness and discipline become pretty, pliable and decorative. results.title: IWF Korea mentors North Jeolla startups on global expansion
results.content: The International Women's Forum Korea (IWF Korea) held one-on-one mentoring sessions for local startups in North Jeolla Province on Saturday to help them evaluate their business strategies and prepare for overseas expansion. IWF Korea said Tuesday that it hosted the "Local Startup Value-Up: Local to Global" mentoring program in Jeonju, North Jeolla Province. The program was organized as part of the 2026 J-Startup Festa and held in conjunction with the 11th Startup Jeonbuk Entrepreneurship Expo in Jeonju's Hanok Village. It was jointly sponsored by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups, North Jeolla Province and the city of Jeonju, with the Jeonbuk Center for Creative Economy and Innovation, the Jeonbuk Business Agency, investment firm Krypton and IWF Korea participating in its organization. results.title: Samsung supports 1,000 startups, helping attract $1.6 bil. in investment
results.content: Samsung Electronics said Tuesday it has supported 1,000 startups, helping attract a cumulative 2.2 trillion won ($1.6 billion) in investment. Notably, the Korean tech giant selects promising entrepreneurs and startups for its C-Lab initiative, choosing 30 companies this year, the company said. Of the selected startups, 15 are currently conducting technology verification projects with Samsung Electronics, with the company seeking to identify further opportunities for business collaborations. Twelve of the startups are based outside the Seoul metropolitan area, Samsung said. Samsung has operated regional C-Lab hubs in the central city of Daegu and the southwestern city of Gwangju since 2023 to foster regional economic development. results.title: Top court schedules another deliberation for ex-PM's martial law trial, raising likelihood of release
results.content: The Supreme Court on Tuesday scheduled another deliberation session on former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo's appeal on insurrection charges, raising the likelihood of his release when his detention period runs out next week. The top court said it would hold the second deliberation round on Han's appeal on Nov. 19, a day before his six-month detention period expires over his role in former President Yoon Suk Yeol's failed martial law bid. Given the schedule, Han, who was sentenced to 15 years in prison by an appellate court, is likely to be released when his detention period runs out as it can no longer be extended. Supreme Court proceedings for Han's appeal have been drawn out after the court referred the case to its full bench in August, citing the public's high interest and its historical importance. results.title: Lee says Korea will continue cooperation with US administration
results.content: President Lee Jae Myung said Tuesday that Korea will continue to closely cooperate with the U.S. administration following the recent U.S. midterm elections, while also seeking to expand bipartisan support in Congress for issues related to the country and the alliance. Lee made the remarks at a Cabinet meeting after the opposition Democratic Party in the United States won control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in last week's midterm elections. "After the U.S. midterm elections, many changes are expected to take place in the external environment," the Korean president said, instructing officials to prepare thoroughly for any possible changes. "Utmost attention should be paid to minimizing negative effects from external uncertainties on the domestic economy." "More important than anything would be strengthening and expanding the foundation for cooperation and trust betw

results.title: Military drone crashes in Gimpo; no civilian damage reported: Army
results.content: A small military drone operated by an Army unit crashed in a park in Gimpo, just west of Seoul, on Tuesday morning, with an investigation under way to determine the exact cause, the Army said. No civilian damage was reported. The unmanned vehicle hit the ground following a suspected communication failure during training and was later retrieved, the Army said in a notice to media. "No casualties or civilian damage have been reported, other than the damage to the aircraft itself," Army spokesperson Capt. Bae Seok-jin said in a press briefing. "The military is currently investigating the exact circumstances and cause of the incident." Bae dismissed speculation connecting the crash to North Korea, saying it occurred during training. Gimpo city officials earlier said military authorities were examining the object to determine whether it may be linked to North Korea.

results.title: Hanwha Aerospace secures Korea's 1st approval for vessel-use hydrogen fuel cell
results.content: Hanwha Aerospace said Tuesday it has become the first company in Korea to win type approval for a marine hydrogen fuel cell from the Korean Register, the country’s ship classification society. The company said this is only the fifth time worldwide that a classification society has granted type approval to a hydrogen fuel cell for ships. Classification societies are independent bodies that set and enforce technical standards for how ships are built and operated. Type approval certifies that a product meets international maritime standards and the society’s own rules. Without it, a hydrogen fuel cell cannot be installed on ships or on offshore structures such as drilling vessels. To receive approval, the manufacturer must prove both performance and safety in harsh sea conditions. Hanwha Aerospace said its system passed marine environment tests for conditions such as vibration and tilting.

results.title: POSCO International completes $700 mil. LNG terminal expansion in Gwangyang
results.content: POSCO International, the energy and trading arm of POSCO Group, completed its second liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal in Gwangyang, cementing its position as Korea's top private natural gas operator and reinforcing domestic supply lines. The company held a completion ceremony Tuesday at the Gwangyang LNG terminal, attended by about 100 people, including government officials, business representatives and executives from POSCO Group. The project cost 949.2 billion won ($700 million) and took 47 months to complete, adding two storage tanks, each with a capacity of 200,000 cubic meters, along with supporting facilities. The development also includes a berth capable of accommodating LNG carriers with capacities of up to 270,000 cubic meters and a separate bunkering berth for vessels of up to 20,000 cubic meters. results.title: Everland's newest panda Shubao draws 50,000 visitors in 10 days
results.content: Shubao, the youngest giant panda at Everland, has drawn about 50,000 visitors in roughly 10 days since she first went on public view, the theme park’s operator said Tuesday. Samsung C&T’s resort division, which runs Everland in Yongin, Gyeonggi Province, said the cub began appearing at the park’s Panda World enclosure on Oct. 30. She was on view for about an hour a day in her first week. Everland has since raised that to three to four hours as she gets used to visitors. Shubao was born June 3 to mother Aibao and father Lebao. She is the fourth giant panda born in Korea, after Fubao in 2020 and twins Ruibao and Huibao in 2023. Fubao moved to China in April 2024. Crowds are also coming to see the twins before they leave for China in the third week of December. results.title: Cha Eun-woo spotted riding Seoul subway in military uniform
results.content: ASTRO member and actor Cha Eun-woo has once again drawn attention during his mandatory military service, this time after a video apparently showing him riding a Seoul subway train in uniform went viral online. The footage, reportedly filmed by a fan while on Seoul Metro Line 4, has circulated widely across social media and online communities. It shows a man believed to be Cha standing among ordinary passengers, wearing a military uniform and a cap pulled low over his face. Despite the cap, his distinctive facial features and sharp jawline caught viewers' attention. The overseas fan who uploaded the video said they initially told an acquaintance that the man resembled Cha, only to be told that it was actually the K-pop star. results.title: From NYC to Tokyo: aespa, RIIZE lead Seoul's international tourism push
results.content: Seoul is taking its tourism pitch to some of the world's busiest streets, with K-pop stars leading an international advertising campaign spanning seven cities, including New York, Tokyo and Bangkok. The Seoul Metropolitan Government and Seoul Tourism Organization said they are rolling out large-scale outdoor advertisements for their global campaign, "Absolutely in Seoul," featuring Karina and Winter of girl group aespa, along with boy band RIIZE, at prominent commercial and tourist destinations overseas. Built around the concept of "Seoul Syndrome," the campaign presents Seoul as a place where ordinary experiences become extraordinary, capturing the lasting impression the city leaves on visitors and their desire to return. results.title: Korean NPU maker DEEPX's new chip wins CES Innovation Award
results.content: Korean neural processing unit (NPU) developer DEEPX's new artificial intelligence (AI) chip has been named a CES 2027 Innovation Awards honoree in the AI category, the company said Tuesday. The CES Innovation Awards recognize products based on their technological capabilities, design and innovation. The award-winning chip is DX-M2, an ultra-low-power generative AI chip designed to run large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) directly on robots and industrial devices. It is built on Samsung Electronics' 2-nanometer foundry process and designed to perform generative AI inference while consuming approximately 5 watts of power. While conventional on-device AI chips primarily focus on image recognition and object detection, the DX-M2 is designed to enable devices to understand their surroundings and make decisions using generative AI. results.title: Korea, US hold combined air resupply exercise for wartime readiness
results.content: Korea and the United States conducted Tuesday a combined aerial resupply exercise aimed at bolstering their capabilities for rapid airborne logistics supply in wartime scenarios, the allies' combined forces said. The exercise, led by the Korea-U.S. Combined Forces Command (CFC), is designed to maintain rapid aerial sustainment capabilities using combined air transport assets when ground resupply routes are compromised during wartime, the CFC said in a release. The latest drills focused on air-drop operations delivering both heavy loads and light supplies. In particular, forces practiced cross-aerial resupply of military hardware and equipment around the clock and from varying altitudes of more than 3,000 meters, the CFC said. results.title: Top diplomats of Korea, France discuss ties, Ukraine war
results.content: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun has met his French counterpart in Paris and discussed bilateral ties and international issues, including the war in Ukraine, Seoul's foreign ministry said Tuesday. Cho held talks with French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot on Monday (local time) on the sidelines of a Group of Seven (G7) foreign ministers' meeting, according to the ministry. The two reviewed relations that were elevated to a "strategic partnership" this year, the 140th anniversary of diplomatic ties, and agreed to expand practical and mutually beneficial cooperation in areas, such as high-tech industries. Cho asked France to continue its support for and interest in Korean companies doing business in Europe. results.title: TXT to turn Lotte World into 'Magic Land' for 1,000 fans
results.content: K-pop group TOMORROW X TOGETHER (TXT) is taking over Seoul’s Lotte World Adventure later this month, shutting down the theme park to host an exclusive comeback celebration for 1,000 fans. The five-member group announced Monday that it will host “TOMORROW X TOGETHER in MAGIC LAND” on Nov. 30 to celebrate the release of its ninth mini album, “PERFECT STORM.” The event will welcome members of MOA, the group's official fandom, to Lotte World Adventure in Jamsil, southeastern Seoul, for a two-part program combining live music and theme park attractions. Part one will feature a performance by TXT, while part two will give participants access to the indoor amusement park facilities. Adding to the occasion, all five members will take on roles as theme park cast members, allowing them to interact more closely with fans and share the experience. results.title: The meaning of US midterm elections
results.content: The resounding defeat of Republicans in the midterm elections has reshaped the political dynamics of the United States. It has also raised questions about what this shift in political power means for agreements Korea concluded with the Donald Trump administration. In the short term, the only certainty is that the election results will create greater uncertainty in dealing with the U.S. The real question for policymakers is what these shifts may mean for U.S. policy over the medium to long term. Policymakers in Korea need to view the elections through the lens of both their immediate implications and the broader trajectory of U.S. politics. results.title: Int'l Memorial Day for UN Korean War veterans to be held in Busan
results.content: An annual international commemoration will take place in the South Korean city of Busan later this week to remember U.N. veterans fallen during the 1950-53 Korean War, the veterans ministry said Tuesday. The International Memorial Day for U.N. Korean War Veterans is scheduled to be held at the U.N. Memorial Cemetery in Korea in the port city, some 330 kilometers southeast of Seoul, on Wednesday, the ministry said in a release. Seoul hosts the event Nov. 11 every year to honor the veterans who fought alongside South Korean forces under the U.N. flag against the Soviet-backed North Korea during the three-year conflict. The war ended in an armistice, not a peace treaty. results.title: N. Korea's Kim stresses importance of agriculture, vows to improve rural life
results.content: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un has emphasized the importance of agriculture and pledged to improve living standards in rural areas, state media said Tuesday. Kim spoke on Monday during a photo session with participants in the 10th Congress of the Union of Agricultural Workers of Korea (UAWK), the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported. He praised the workers for boosting grain production and stressed the party "remains unshakable in its plan and decision to make the faithful agricultural workers enjoy the benefits of ideal society, highly civilized and prosperous, earlier than anyone else." He also called on the union to "play the role of the ideological agitator and vanguard that accelerates the rural development," describing it as the union's "primary duty." results.title: KRX activates buy-side sidecar for KOSPI on sharp rise
results.content: Korea's bourse operator on Tuesday activated a buy-side sidecar for the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) as the stock index rose sharply. Program trading for the KOSPI-listed shares was suspended for five minutes at 9:06 a.m., according to the Korea Exchange (KRX). After opening 4.55 percent higher, the KOSPI added 240.01 points, or 4.78 percent, to 5,258.86 as of 9:10 a.m. The index rallied on strong tech gains following overnight gains on Wall Street driven by eased military tensions in the Middle East. A buy-side sidecar is triggered when the KOSPI 200 Futures Index rises 5 percent or more for at least one minute.
